reason: V3 materially reduces flats, losses and weekly drawdown but sacrifices too much endpoint return, profit factor, rolling-window performance and event-equity drawdown versus locked V2.
interpretation: The runway/continuation concept is validated as a flat-monetization mechanism: modeled campaigns eliminated all flats; the 26 remaining flats are only insufficient-history V2 fallback trades.
The 30% extraction risk haircut is too broad because EXTRACTION contains a large amount of positive expectancy and dominates selected trades.

Adaptive banking is too aggressive on right-tail winners: it recovered +73.4625R from common flats but surrendered -92.2903R from common winners, including -48.0171R from common V2 trades that had realized at least 3R.

The next refinement should preserve the V2 baseline and retain runway intelligence while decoupling entry classification from blanket risk reduction and making banking more continuation-decay selective so right-tail runners remain effectively untaxed.
No global 3R ceiling should be restored.
